summary: Chengdu is well suited for food-focused, low-pressure city travel with walkable historic districts, tea-house culture, and strong neighborhood character.
transport_notes: Central Chengdu works well with metro rides plus short walks.
Keep the itinerary clustered by district to avoid unnecessary cross-city movement.
Evening activities work best when they stay near food streets or riverwalk zones.

budget_notes.low: Prioritize snack streets, public transit, and compact walking districts.
budget_notes.medium: Mix classic neighborhoods, signature food areas, and one or two slower cultural stops.
budget_notes.high: Add more refined dining and slower, comfort-oriented breaks without overpacking the day.

trip_type_notes.student: Student trips should feel affordable, lively, and easy to execute without private transport.
trip_type_notes.solo: Solo plans should feel flexible and safe with clear district logic.
trip_type_notes.couple: Couple plans should balance atmosphere, food, and relaxed evening pacing.
trip_type_notes.family: Family plans should avoid excessive transfers and long high-density walking blocks.
